the tetracyclineresistant promoter tcp830 can be used to induce the biosynthesis of novobiocins in S. coelicolor M 512.
the tetracyclin-inducible promoter system tcp830 can be used for the heterologous production of novobiocins.
the tetracyclin-inducible tcp830 promoter is a robust and versatile system for the production of secondary metabolites in heterologous producers.

a new approach for the production of secondary metabolites in heterologous producers.
the use of the tcp830 promoter for the heterologous production of novobiocins.

the tcp830 promoter is an excellent choice for inducible expression in heterologous streptomycetes.
the tcp830 promoter is an excellent tool for inducible expression in S. coelicolor.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tcp830 promoter can be used to achieve high-level expression of biosynthesic gene clusters in heterlogous hosts.
the tcp830 promoter is a robust, easy to use system for inducible expression in heterologous producers.

we have developed a system to express heterologous biosynthetic genes at a very high level and at any time during the growth phase of the host organism, thus enabling the production of secondary metabolites with an optimized titer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tcp830 promoter can be used to increase the production of secondary metabolites in heterologous strains, and that this can be achieved by using a single tcp830 insertion.
the tcp830 promoter can be used for the inducibly controlled expression of large biosynthetic gene loci.
it is feasible to replace the natural promoter of a biosynthetic gene locus with a strong, heterologous promoter without losing production of the target antibiotic.
